solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Juliet imprisoned in castle keeps unsettling workers on roof

indicators.note: being imprisoned in something means being shut inside it, so one letter goes within the others
unsettling the words castle and keeps throws their letters into a new order

parts.note: J is Juliet in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet locked in a castle is unnerving the men repairing its roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettling' shuffles CASTLE KEEPS, and 'imprisoned in' puts J (Juliet) among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeplejacks are tradesmen who climb and repair church spires, chimneys and high roofs.

clue.text: Farewell to old pipe, sadly

indicators.note: sadly here means badly or in a sorry state, so the letters of old and pipe come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone mournfully saying goodbye to their old tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Toodle-pip is a jaunty, old-fashioned British way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Raise each napkin initially, and peer underneath

indicators.note: in a down answer, what lies underneath comes after the earlier letters
initially points to the opening letters of the words each and napkin

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, a noble

explanation.surface: Instructions for a dinner: lift every napkin and look beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peer' looks like a verb meaning look closely, but it is a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the peerage, elevating their rank.

clue.text: A native American, I'll ask for that regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every second letter of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone politely offers to ask on another person's behalf, over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of ILLASKFORTHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lakota are a Sioux people of the Great Plains, so a member of the tribe is a native American.

clue.text: Possible Welshman's skeleton with a different head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is swapped for another

parts.note: a skeleton is a set of bones

explanation.surface: A Welshman's skeleton found with someone else's skull.
explanation.walkthrough: BONES changes its first letter to J; the clue leaves the solver to find which letter makes a Welsh name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jones is among the commonest surnames in Wales, so a man so called is quite possibly Welsh.

clue.text: Copper lead ultimately is something to chew on

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word lead

explanation.surface: Copper and lead as metals, one of them oddly described as chewable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' is the metal in the surface, but only its last letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: Cud is the partly digested food that cows bring back up and chew again.

clue.text: What we have in common is military training

indicators.note: training licks something into a new shape, so the letters of is and military are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people agreeing that the thing they share is army training.
explanation.definitionFit: A similarity is a shared feature or likeness between people or things.

clue.text: Old monarch at first just omits his name

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: An old king who, oddly, leaves out his own name.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a riddle about the monarch's name; the four words simply spell it with their initials.
explanation.definitionFit: King John reigned over England from 1199 to 1216, a monarch of long ago.

clue.text: No good to perform in Kim's realm

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the name

parts.note: the name Kim, the possessive serving only the surface

explanation.surface: Someone is useless at putting on a show in Kim's country.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim suggests Korea's Kim dynasty; here the name is just a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingdom is a realm ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: A tiny bit secure in Kent town

parts.note: a whit is the smallest amount, as in 'not a whit'
secure means firm or steady, stable

explanation.surface: A town in Kent described as slightly safe.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitstable is a seaside town in the English county of Kent, famous for oysters.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitstable is a coastal town in the county of Kent on the north Kent shore.

clue.text: Something fishy a politician kept in shed

indicators.note: something kept in a place is held inside it

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician

explanation.surface: A suspicious matter: a politician locked in a shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fishy' suggests something dodgy, but the answer is a real fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish, so it is literally something fishy.

clue.text: One used to make spirits all the same

definitions.meaning: first meaning: apparatus for distilling alcohol

explanation.walkthrough: 'spirits' hints at ghosts, but these are distilled drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A still is distilling equipment for whisky or gin, and 'still' as an adverb means nonetheless.

clue.text: How baked beans are sold? About right, so, for native

indicators.note: about means around, so the first letters go round the next one

parts.note: baked beans come in a tin, so they are sold in tin
sic is Latin for so or thus

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about tinned beans, then a scrap of instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: Baked beans are sold in a tin; 'native' here means inborn or inherent, not a local person.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrinsic qualities are inherent or native to something, belonging to its essential nature.

clue.text: Salesperson Pat returns: he knocks

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman called Pat comes back and knocks at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: REP followed by PAT, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapper is someone who taps, that is a person who knocks lightly.

clue.text: One sharing billing with new actors

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters of actors are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A performer sharing top billing alongside some newcomers.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star appears with equal prominence on a film or theatre bill alongside another lead.

clue.text: What bridge player may do in proverb, ideally

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words proverb ideally

explanation.surface: A proverb about ideal conduct for a bridge player.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of PROVERB and IDEALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game bridge, to overbid is to bid more than one's hand justifies.

clue.text: PS: on reflection, wet weather can cause injury

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters of PS are turned round

explanation.surface: A postscript warning that wet weather can lead to an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can cause' links the wordplay to the definition; slippery rain may lead to a twisted ankle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is an injury from wrenching a joint's ligaments.

clue.text: It recoils before young dog, upset

indicators.note: before places this ahead of the next piece
something that recoils springs back, so the word it is turned round

parts.note: a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: Something shrinks back from a puppy, distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like an adjective about the pup, but it is the verb meaning overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip up is to overturn or knock over, the verb sense of upset.

clue.text: Climbing mountain, carefully note alternative strategy

indicators.note: in a down answer, climbing means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: NB stands for nota bene, Latin for note well

explanation.surface: Advice for a mountaineer to make a careful note of a fallback route.
explanation.definitionFit: Plan B is the backup scheme used if the first plan fails.

clue.text: Second-guess public relations decree

parts.note: an edict is an official decree

explanation.surface: Doubting an official decree issued by a press office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second-guess' usually means doubt in hindsight, but here it means guess ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To second-guess can mean to anticipate what will happen, that is to forecast.

clue.text: Neckerchief found in club — and an anorak

indicators.note: found in tells the solver the letters are inside the phrase club and an anorak

explanation.surface: A neck scarf turned up in a club along with a waterproof jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash in the clue is ignored; the letters run from cluB AND AN Anorak.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large coloured handkerchief worn around the neck or head.

clue.text: Dun horse?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dun is to press persistently for payment, to pester
second meaning: an old or worn-out horse

explanation.walkthrough: Dun is a horse colour, so the surface reads as one description; but dun is also a verb meaning to badger a debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag is to pester repeatedly, as a creditor duns, and a nag is an old horse.

clue.text: Party attempt a big hit

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate meanings of one short word sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Bash means a party, a go at something, and a hard strike.

clue.text: Crazy eg ceding best dish

indicators.note: crazy means wild or mad, so the letters of ceding and best are scrambled

explanation.surface: An odd instruction about giving up the best of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs Benedict is a breakfast dish of poached eggs and ham on muffins with hollandaise.
